Whatever is like this, the preponderance of its existence over its non-existence, or of its non-existence over its existence, must be by the influence and preponderance of the Necessary Existent. Thus the influence of His power in bringing it into being and annihilating it is executed and pervasive, without any resistance at all. The first: it is derived from madda al-shay'a (he stretched the thing) so that it extended, namely that its mountains are removed by being blown away, as He said: ﴿They ask you about the mountains. As for His saying ﴿and hears and obeys its Lord, as it must﴾, its explanation has already passed, except that the first is about the sky and this is about the earth, and when the sense of the discourse differs, it is not a repetition.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 84, verse 6:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet Him﴾.

Know that His saying, exalted is He, ﴿When the sky splits open﴾ up to His saying ﴿O mankind﴾, is a conditional clause (shart), and it necessarily requires an apodosis (jawab). The scholars differed about it in several ways.

The first: The author of al-Kashshaf said: the apodosis of "idha" (when) has been omitted so that the mind may go to every possible thing, which makes it more effective in producing awe.

The second: Al-Farra' said: the apodosis was left out because this meaning is well known and has been repeated throughout the Qur'an, so it is understood. A parallel to this is His saying, ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾ (al-Qadr: 1), where the mention of the Qur'an is omitted because it has already been explicitly stated in other places.

The third: Some of the verifiers (muhaqqiqun) said: the apodosis is His saying ﴿then you will meet Him﴾, and His saying ﴿O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with toil﴾ is a parenthetical insertion (i'tiraD). It is like the speaker's saying: "When such-and-such is the case, O man, you will then see what good or evil you have done." So it is here. The meaning is: when the Day of Resurrection comes, the human being will encounter his deeds.

The fourth: The meaning is taken as inverted (taqdim wa ta'khir), as if it were said: ﴿O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet Him﴾, and ﴿when the sky splits open﴾ and the Resurrection occurs.

The fifth: Al-Kisa'i said: the apodosis is in His saying ﴿Then as for one who is given his record in his right hand﴾, and His saying ﴿O mankind, indeed you are laboring﴾ is an interposed statement within the speech. The meaning is: when the sky splits open, and such-and-such occurs, ﴿then whoever is given his record in his right hand﴾, he is such-and-such, and whoever is given his record behind his back, he is such-and-such. A parallel to this is His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿If guidance comes to you from Me, then whoever follows My guidance, no fear will there be upon them﴾ (al-Baqarah: 38).

The first: It refers to Muhammad (ﷺ), and the meaning is: you are striving (takdahu) in conveying the messages of God, guiding His servants, and bearing harm from the disbelievers. So rejoice, for you will meet God through this deed, and it is not lost with Him.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 84, verse 7–9:

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then as for him who is given his record in his right hand﴾ ﴿he will be called to a light account﴾ ﴿and will return to his family joyful﴾.

The meaning: as for him who is given the record of his deeds in his right hand, ﴿he will be called to a light account﴾. "Sawfa" (surely, will) from Allah is obligatory, and it is like the saying of the speaker: "Follow me, and we will surely find good," for he does not intend by it doubt, but only intends to soften the speech. The light reckoning is that his deeds are presented to him, and he recognizes that this is an act of obedience and this is an act of disobedience; then he is rewarded for the obedience and overlooked for the disobedience. This is the light reckoning, because there is no severity upon its owner and no scrutiny, and he is not told: "Why did you do this?", nor is he asked for an excuse concerning it or for a proof against him.

For whenever he is held to account for that, he will find no excuse or proof, and so he will be disgraced. Then, at this light reckoning, he returns to his family joyful, victorious with reward, safe from punishment. By "his family" is meant the people of Paradise among the wide-eyed houris, or his wives and offspring if they are believers. This verse indicates that He, glorified is He, has prepared for him and for his family in Paradise what befits him of reward.

"From 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, she said: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: O Allah, call me to account with an easy account.' I said: 'And what is the easy account?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, surely Allah says: ﴿Then as for him who is given his record in his right hand﴾ ﴿he will be called to a light account﴾.' As for His saying: ﴿But as for him who is given his record behind his back﴾, the exegetes have several views on it.

The first: al-Kalbi said: the reason is that his right hand is chained to his neck, and his left hand is behind his back.

The second: Mujahid said: his left hand is dislocated and placed behind his back.

The third: some people said: his face turns around to the back of his neck, so he reads his record in that manner.

The fourth: his record is given to him in his left hand from behind his back, because when he tries to take it with his right hand, as the believers do, he is prevented from doing so, and it is given to him from behind his back in his left hand.

If it is said: Did He not say in Surat al-Haqqah: ﴿But as for him who is given his record in his left hand﴾ [al-Haqqah: 25], without mentioning the back?

The answer is in two respects:

The first: it is possible that he is given it in his left hand from behind his back, according to what we have related from al-Kalbi.

The second: that some of them are given it in their left hand, and some of them from behind their back.

As for His saying ﴿So he will call out for destruction﴾:

Know that thubur (destruction) is ruin, and the meaning is that when he is given his record not in his right hand, he knows that he is among the people of the Fire, so he says: "Wa-thuburah!" (Woe to me, destruction!). Al-Farra' said: the Arabs say "Fulan yad'u lahfahu" (so-and-so calls out his lahf) when he says: "Wa-lahfah!" (Alas!).

There is another view, mentioned by al-Qaffal, who said: thubur is derived from al-muthabarah ʿala shay' (persistence in something), which is constant attention to it. The ruin of the Hereafter is called thubur because it is constant and does not cease, as He said: ﴿Indeed, its punishment is ever adhering (gharam)﴾ [al-Furqan: 65]. The root of gharam is adherence and clinging.

That is because first it will be split, as He said: ﴿When the sky splits open﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 1], then it will be cleft, as He said: ﴿When the sky is cleft asunder﴾ [al-Infitar: 1], then it will become ﴿red like oil-dregs﴾ [al-Rahman: 37], and at times ﴿like molten brass﴾ [al-Maʿarij: 8], as Allah Most High mentioned these things in verses of the Qur'an. So it is as if, when He mentioned at the beginning of the surah that it will split, He swore at the end of the surah that it changes from state to state. This view is narrated from Ibn Masʿud.

The third issue: His saying, ﴿stage from stage﴾, means after a stage, as in the poet's words:

I kept crossing one watering place after another, until I camped at the door of ʿAbd al-Wahid.

The reasoning for this is that when a person moves from one thing to another thing, he has arrived at the second after the first, so baʿd and ʿan are suitable as alternatives. Also, the word ʿan indicates distance and passing beyond, so it was similar to the word baʿd.

As for His saying, ﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe?﴾, there are two issues in it:

The first issue: the more likely meaning of ﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe﴾ is belief in the truth of resurrection (al-ba'th) and the Last Day. This is because He, exalted is He, related of the disbeliever: ﴿Indeed, he thought that he would never return﴾, then He, glorified is He, ruled that he would return. When He then said, ﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe﴾, this indicates that the meaning is: ﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe﴾ in resurrection and the Last Day. Furthermore, know that His saying ﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe﴾ is a question in the sense of denunciation (al-inkar), and this is only fitting when the proof has become manifest and the doubts have been removed. The matter here is so, because He, glorified is He, swore by changes occurring in the celestial spheres and the elements. Indeed, al-shafaq (the afterglow of twilight) is a state different from what precedes it, which is the light of day, and from what follows it, which is the darkness of night. Likewise His saying ﴿And by the night and what it gathers﴾ indicates the occurrence of darkness after light, and the change of the states of animals from wakefulness to sleep. Likewise His saying ﴿And by the moon when it becomes full﴾ indicates the attainment of the moon's completeness after it had been deficient. He, exalted is He, swore by these changing states to indicate the change of the states of creation, and this definitively indicates the soundness of the doctrine of resurrection, because the One who is capable of changing the upper and lower bodies from state to state and attribute to attribute according to what is beneficial must, in Himself, be capable of all possibilities and knowing of all knowables. Whoever is like this is without doubt capable of resurrection and the Last Day. Since what precedes this verse serves as a decisive rational proof for the soundness of resurrection and the Last Day, He rightly said, by way of astonishment: ﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe﴾.

The second issue: al-Qadi said: It is not permissible for the Wise to say, concerning one who is incapable of faith, ﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe﴾. Since He said this, it indicates that they are capable, and this requires that the capacity (al-istita'ah) precede the act, that they be the originators of their own acts, and that He, exalted is He, not be the creator of disbelief in them. This verse is therefore among the clear (muhkamat) verses which admit no possibility of other meaning at all, and its answer has already been given more than once.

صفحة ١٠٢

**The Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 84, Verse 21**

Regarding His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate﴾, there are several issues:

**The first issue:** They were masters of eloquence and rhetoric, so when they heard the Qur'an they must have known that it is a miracle (mu'jiz). Once they knew the truth of Muhammad's (ﷺ) prophethood and the obligation to obey him in his commands and prohibitions, Allah deemed it greatly blameworthy of them that, upon hearing the Qur'an, they abandoned prostration and obedience.

**The second issue:** Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, 'Ata', al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: the intended meaning of "prostration" is prayer (salah). Abu Muslim said: it is humility and submission. Others said: rather, the intended meaning is the actual prostration at specific verses, and this verse is one of them.

**The third issue:** It is reported that he (ﷺ) recited one day: ﴿Prostrate and draw near﴾ [al-'Alaq: 19], and he prostrated, as did the believers who were with him, while Quraysh were clapping above their heads and whistling. Then this verse was revealed. Abu Hanifa argued from this for the obligation of the prostration in two ways:

The first: that his (ﷺ) action necessitates obligation, based on the words of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿And follow him﴾ [al-A'raf: 158].

The second: that Allah, Exalted is He, censured those who hear it and do not prostrate, and the occurrence of censure upon abandoning it indicates obligation.

**The fourth issue:** The view of Ibn 'Abbas is that there is no prostration in al-Mufassal (the final short surahs of the Qur'an). It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah that he prostrated here and said: "By Allah, I did not prostrate in it except after I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prostrate in it." It is narrated from Anas: "I prayed behind Abu Bakr, 'Umar and 'Uthman, and they prostrated." And from al-Hasan: it is not obligatory.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 84, verse 22–25:

As for His saying, ﴿Nay, those who disbelieve deny it﴾, the meaning is that the proofs which necessitate faith, although they are clear and manifest, the disbelievers nonetheless deny them, either out of blind imitation of their forefathers (taqlid), or out of envy, or out of fear that if they openly professed faith, the positions and benefits of this world would escape them.

As for His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And Allah knows best what they conceal﴾, the root of the word comes from the wi'a (receptacle). It is said: awa'tu al-shay', meaning I put the thing into a receptacle, as in His saying: ﴿And he gathered [wealth] and hoarded it﴾ (fa-awa). And Allah knows best what they gather in their breasts of polytheism and denial, so He will requite them for it in this world and the Hereafter.

* * *

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾, which they deserve because of their denial and disbelief.

As for His saying: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward that will never end﴾, there are two opinions concerning it.

The author of al-Kashshaf said: the exception is disjunctive (munqati'), and he said: most scholars hold that its meaning is "except those among them who repent," for they, although they are disbelievers at present, once they repent, believe, and do righteous deeds, then for them is a reward, which is the great reward.

Regarding the meaning of ﴿never-ending﴾ (ghayr mamnun), there are several aspects:

First: that this reward reaches them without reproach or harm.

Second: without interruption.

Third: without disturbance.

Fourth: without diminution. The better view is to take the expression as covering all of these, because one of the conditions of reward is the attainment of all of them. It is as though He, may He be exalted, promised them a reward pure of all impurities, lasting, without cessation, decrease, or deficiency, and this is the utmost of promise. Thus that became an encouragement to acts of worship, just as what preceded it is a deterrent from sins. And Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best, and all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
